slides.p: They block beta-adrenergic receptors, so heart rate and force of contraction fall.
Atenolol and metoprolol are beta-1 selective. Propranolol is non-selective. Carvedilol also blocks alpha-1.
Avoid in asthma and severe bradycardia. Do not stop suddenly, because rebound tachycardia and hypertension can occur.

subject: Pharmacology
q: Which of these is an ACE inhibitor?
ex: Captopril blocks angiotensin-converting enzyme. Losartan blocks the AT1 receptor instead.

subject: Pharmacology
back: N-acetylcysteine (NAC). It replenishes glutathione, which detoxifies the toxic metabolite.

subject: Pharmacology
title: Grapefruit and statins
p: Grapefruit juice inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, which can raise blood levels of drugs such as simvastatin.

slides.p: The fraction of a dose that reaches the systemic circulation unchanged. An IV dose is 100%.
Solubility, first-pass metabolism, dosage form and food.
Compare the AUC of the oral dose with the AUC of an IV dose, adjusted for the doses given.

subject: Pharmaceutics
q: Which coating protects a drug from stomach acid?
ex: Enteric coatings resist gastric acid and dissolve at the higher pH of the intestine.

subject: Pharmaceutics
front: What does the HLB value describe?
back: The hydrophilic-lipophilic balance of a surfactant. About 3 to 6 suits W/O emulsifiers and about 8 to 18 suits O/W emulsifiers.

subject: Pharmaceutics
title: Dissolution can limit absorption
p: For poorly soluble drugs (BCS class II), how fast the drug dissolves is often what limits absorption.

slides.p: Starts with blood vessel changes and neutrophils arriving at the site.
Redness, heat, swelling, pain and loss of function.
Dominated by macrophages and lymphocytes. Granulomas are a classic example, as in tuberculosis.

subject: Pathology
q: Which cell predominates early in acute inflammation?
ex: Neutrophils arrive first. Macrophages and lymphocytes dominate later, in chronic inflammation.

subject: Pathology
back: Necrosis is uncontrolled cell death with inflammation. Apoptosis is programmed, energy-dependent death without inflammation.

subject: Pathology
title: What a granuloma is
p: A granuloma is a cluster of activated macrophages called epithelioid cells, typical of tuberculosis.

slides.p: Some drugs have a narrow therapeutic index, so small dose changes matter.
Digoxin, lithium, phenytoin, vancomycin and aminoglycosides.
Take a trough level just before the next dose, once steady state is reached.

subject: Clinical Pharmacy
q: About how many half-lives are needed to reach steady state?
ex: With repeated dosing, steady state is reached after roughly 4 to 5 half-lives.

subject: Clinical Pharmacy
back: With the INR. The target is usually 2 to 3 for most indications.

subject: Clinical Pharmacy
title: Type A reactions
p: Type A adverse drug reactions are dose-related and predictable from the drug's pharmacology.

slides.p: Willow bark gave salicin, which leads to salicylic acid.
Acetylating salicylic acid gave aspirin, which is easier on the stomach.
It irreversibly acetylates COX enzymes. Low doses block platelet thromboxane A2, and platelets cannot make new enzyme.

subject: Medicinal Chemistry
q: What does a prodrug need before it works?
o: Conversion in the body to the active form
ex: A prodrug is inactive until it is converted by metabolism or chemistry in the body.

subject: Medicinal Chemistry
back: A guide to oral drug-likeness: molecular weight up to 500, logP up to 5, up to 5 H-bond donors and up to 10 acceptors.

subject: Medicinal Chemistry
title: The beta-lactam ring
p: The beta-lactam ring is the key part of penicillin. Beta-lactamase enzymes open it, which causes resistance.

slides.p: Basic, nitrogen-containing compounds made by plants.
Morphine from opium poppy, quinine from cinchona, atropine from belladonna, caffeine from coffee.
Dragendorff's and Mayer's reagents give precipitates with alkaloids.

subject: Pharmacognosy
q: Digoxin is obtained from which plant?
ex: Digoxin comes from Digitalis lanata, the foxglove. Quinine is from cinchona and reserpine from Rauwolfia.

subject: Pharmacognosy
back: Cinchona bark. It is used as an antimalarial.

subject: Pharmacognosy
title: An early antihypertensive
p: Reserpine, from Rauwolfia serpentina, was one of the first drugs used to treat high blood pressure.
